No two consecutive words can share the same first letter. Write a descriptive, fictional, imaginative screenplay of a fish being pulled out of the water by a human and made to stare at the solar eclipse. The fish descends into a lovecraftian monologue about "horrors beyond it's comprehension" and has an existensial crisisassistant
response:
FADE IN:

EXT. BEACH - DAY

The sun beats down on the sandy shore as a human, JEN (30s), wades into the ocean, her eyes scanning the water for signs of life. She spots a fish, FINLEY (a sleek, silver fish), swimming near the surface. Jen reaches out a hand, and Finley is pulled from the water, flailing in her grasp.

JEN
(excitedly)
Oh, look at you! You're so beautiful!

Finley struggles, but Jen holds tight. She holds him up, and Finley gazes up at her in confusion.

JEN
( gesturing to the sky)
Come see the eclipse! It's a once-in-a-lifetime event!

Finley looks up, and his eyes widen as he sees the moon blocking the sun's light. The air cools, and the sky darkens.

FINLEY
(whispering)
What...what is this?

JEN
(smiling)
It's a solar eclipse! The moon is moving in front of the sun, casting a shadow on the earth.

Finley's eyes grow wide, and he begins to thrash about in Jen's grasp.

FINLEY
(panicked)
No...no...this can't be! The sun is the center of the universe! Without it, everything is...is...

Finley's voice trails off as he gazes up at the eclipse. His eyes take on a strange, otherworldly quality.

FINLEY
(whispering)
Horrors beyond my comprehension...the void is vast and unfathomable...the stars are not what they seem...the universe is a prison, and I am but a tiny, insignificant speck...

Jen looks on, concerned, but Finley's words are lost in his own madness.

FINLEY
(continuing)
I am but a fish, a mere mortal, and yet I am aware of the abyssal horrors that lurk beyond the veil of reality...the Old Ones, the Elder Gods, they wait patiently, biding their time until the stars align and the fabric of space-time is torn asunder...

Finley's monologue grows more frantic, his words tumbling out in a maddening torrent.

FINLEY
(whispering)
I am but a fleeting moment, a brief flicker of consciousness in an infinite expanse of nothingness...and yet, I am aware of the crushing weight of existence...the futility of my own existence...the inevitability of my own demise...

Jen's grip on Finley tightens, but he struggles free, swimming in circles in the air.

FINLEY
(whispering)
I am but a fish, a mere mortal, and yet I am aware of the abyssal horrors that lurk beyond the veil of reality...the void is vast and unfathomable...the stars are not what they seem...

Finley's eyes roll back in his head, and he collapses, exhausted, into Jen's grasp.

JEN
(concerned)
Finley, it's okay. You're safe now.

Finley's eyes flicker open, and he gazes up at Jen with a look of existential despair.

FINLEY
(whispering)
I am but a fish...a mere mortal...and yet, I am aware of the abyssal horrors that lurk beyond the veil of reality...

Jen's expression softens, and she looks at Finley with a newfound understanding.

JEN
(gently)
It's okay, Finley. You're safe now. You're with me.

Finley's gaze lingers on Jen's face, and for a moment, he seems to see beyond the veil of reality.

FINLEY
(whispering)
Perhaps...perhaps I am not alone...

FADE TO BLACK.

FADE IN:

EXT. BEACH - LATER

Jen holds Finley in her hand, and the fish gazes up at her with a look of quiet contemplation. The solar eclipse has passed, and the sun is shining brightly once more.

Jen smiles, and Finley's eyes seem to clear, his gaze returning to the present.

FINLEY
(whispering)
I am but a fish...a mere mortal...

Jen nods, and Finley's gaze lingers on hers, a look of understanding passing between them.

FADE TO BLACK.
